title: Water-modulated conformational heterogeneity underlies multiple timescales of primary charge separation in photosystem II
task: Model multi-exponential kinetics of primary charge separation in Photosystem II
key_results: Water-modulated conformational heterogeneity explains multi-exponential behavior; apparent lifetimes <250 fs, 386 fs, 2.7 ps match experimental data
comments: Elegant reconciliation of conflicting prior assignments through protein-solvent dynamics; quantum-classical coupling details and validation against additional experimental probes would strengthen conclusions.

model_io.model: Atomistic molecular dynamics + quantum dynamics simulations

hypotheses.hypothesis: Multi-exponential charge separation kinetics arise from parallel chemically distinct intermediate pathways
hypotheses.result: Rejected; water-modulated conformational heterogeneity provides better explanation

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dynamic water channels and protein fluctuations near oxygen-evolving complex govern multi-exponential kinetics via single Chl_D1+ Pheo_D1- intermediate pathway
hypotheses.result: Confirmed by kinetic modeling with lifetimes matching experimental data

title: Structural basis of nonmuscle myosin-2 autoinhibition mechanisms

key_results: 53-nm elongated full-length NM2B structure; tri-segmented tail fold that sequesters actin-binding and filament-assembly interfaces
comments: High-resolution structural insights into a functionally critical autoinhibited state; disease-relevance strengthens translational potential but mechanism of regulatory PTM effects requires further validation.

model_io.model: Cryo-EM structural determination

hypotheses.hypothesis: Tri-segmented tail fold sequesters actin-binding and filament-assembly interfaces in 10S state
hypotheses.result: Confirmed by cryo-EM structural analysis

hypotheses.hypothesis: Asymmetric arrangement of heavy and light chains mechanistically explains conformational equilibrium shifts under PTMs and mutations
hypotheses.result: Supported by structural observations; provides framework for future mechanistic studies

title: SPOP-mediated nuclear ubiquitination degradation of p62/SQSTM1 contributes to HR repair
task: Determine SPOP-mediated p62/SQSTM1 degradation mechanism in homologous recombination repair
key_results: Nuclear DNA damage enhances SPOP-p62 interaction; SPOP catalyzes p62 ubiquitination at K7, triggering degradation and upregulating RAD51/FLNA; patient-derived p62 SBC-motif mutations (S276Y/S277G/S277I) increase radiotherapy sensitivity via HR deficiency
comments: Mechanistic dissection of SPOP-p62 ubiquitination in HR is precise, though biological significance of nuclear vs. cytoplasmic p62 degradation in different stress contexts requires clarification.

model_io.model: Cancer cells with DNA damage ± patient-derived p62 mutations
Xenograft tumors with p62 SBC-motif mutations

hypotheses.hypothesis: SPOP catalyzes nuclear p62 ubiquitination at K7 in response to DNA damage

hypotheses.hypothesis: p62 K7 ubiquitination leads to RAD51/FLNA upregulation and enhanced HR
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; p62 degradation increases both proteins and HR foci

hypotheses.hypothesis: Patient p62 SBC-motif mutations impair SPOP binding and increase radiotherapy resistance

hypotheses.hypothesis: LRRC8A disruption impairs KRAS/EGFR signaling and ribosome biogenesis

title: Fas acts as a T cell co-stimulatory receptor via both death domain-independent and -dependent mechanisms

key_results: Fas concentrates at immune synapse and lowers TCR activation threshold via DD-independent mechanism; DD-dependent cascade (FADD-caspase-8-RIPK1-TAK1) initiates gene-activating pathways; caspase-8 inhibition favors RIPK1-dependent co-stimulation
comments: Multi-level integration of Fas into TCR signaling is mechanistically detailed, but distinction between caspase-8's pro-death vs. pro-stimulation roles depends on kinetic context requiring further validation.

model_io.model: T cell activation with Fas/FasL (TCR + APC)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Fas DD-independent mechanism lowers TCR threshold

hypotheses.hypothesis: Caspase-8 inhibition blocks both death and co-stimulation
